Default plots for mvgam models

Source: R/plot.mvgam.R
plot.mvgam.Rd

Draws one of the standard views of a fitted model, chosen by type.

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam
plot(
  x,
  type = c("residuals", "smooths", "trend", "factors", "series", "latent_state"),
  series = NULL,
  resp = NULL,
  ndraws = NULL,
  component = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fitted mvgam object.

type

The plot to draw:

"residuals" (default)

Dunn-Smyth residuals of one series against the fitted values, their Q-Q plot, ACF and partial ACF, as pp_check.mvgam() draws them. A series observed at unevenly spaced times shows a semivariogram in place of the ACF and partial ACF. An occ() or nmix() fit has one residual per closure unit and draws the Q-Q plot alone.

"smooths"

The posterior of each smooth, from conditional_smooths.mvgam(), with several smooths combined into one figure.

"trend"

The latent trend over the training times, from hindcast.mvgam(), or the state component component names. A jsdgam() fit has sites in place of times and refuses it.

"factors"

The path of each latent factor. active_factors() reports the variance each factor carries.

"series"

The observed data the fit carries. mvgam_data() plots data before a fit.

"latent_state"

The latent state of an occ() or nmix() fit drawn from the covariates alone: occupancy psi or abundance N, by series and time. A multi-season fit pools the sites of each time.

series

A series index or name. "trend" and "series" also take "all", their default. "residuals" draws one series, the first by default. "smooths", "factors" and "latent_state" ignore it.

resp

Character specifying which response variable for multivariate models. NULL (default) returns predictions for all responses.

ndraws

The number of posterior draws, or NULL for every draw. "residuals" takes 100 by default. "factors" and "series" ignore it.

component

NULL (the default) for the summed trend, or the names of state components of the trend, with type = "trend". Several names give the sum of their components. LLT() has "level", the stochastic level, and "slope", its growth per time step. A seasonal LLT() adds "season". "predictor" holds the effects of the trend formula's covariates. c("level", "predictor") gives the level with those effects. A factor model projects each component through its loadings, as it projects the trend. The result is an ordinary mvgam_forecast-class with the components in its component slot.

...

Further arguments to the function that draws the plot, such as smooths for conditional_smooths.mvgam().

Value

A ggplot object, or a patchwork of several.

See also

forecast.mvgam() and its plot() method draw forecasts. conditional_effects.mvgam() draws covariate effects. mcmc_plot.mvgam() draws posterior diagnostics.

Other model checking: mvgam_diagnostics, pp_check.mvgam(), residuals.mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = poisson(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# Residual diagnostics, the default
plot(mod)


# The smooth of x and the latent AR(1) trend
plot(mod, type = "smooths")

plot(mod, type = "trend")


# The slope of a local linear trend
mod_llt <- update(mod, trend_formula = ~ LLT())
#> Warning: 6 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
plot(mod_llt, type = "trend", component = "slope")


# Next, plot(forecast(mod, newdata = simdat$data_test)) carries the
# trend forward
# }
